messages:
rob: Heads up — CI perf alert on main after today's merges. 18% p99 latency regression on short-seq (<=64) workloads, throughput dip ~12%.

rob: Perf alert link: https://ci.internal/perf/1772

anya: Which PRs were merged this morning?

rob: Two related ones: PR #4187 (kernel-selector: prefer fused-kernel for MHA) commit abcdef1
rob: and PR #4192 (adaptive-batching heuristics) commit fedcba2

kai: Can we bisect? I can run a perf-bisect script on the perf-ci image.

rob: deploy-bot: perf-ci job 177210 -- failed metric: p99_latency_ms: baseline 22.3 -> 26.3 :warning:

sam: Observed KV cache hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 71% on canary traces. Possibly batching + cache eviction interaction.

rob: I started a bisect, quick notes: when we land abcdef1 p99 jumps. But fedcba2 amplifies it. Root cause seems to be kernel selection picking high-throughput kernel that underperforms small batches.

maria: Plan: create a release branch and cherry-pick a minimal revert of abcdef1, keep adaptive-batching to avoid regressions. Steps:
```
git checkout -b release/patch/perf-1772
git revert --no-edit abcdef1
git push origin release/patch/perf-1772
gh pr create --title "perf: revert kernel-selector abcdef1" --base main --head release/patch/perf-1772
```

rob: @kai can you run canary on dedicated with that revert? Need p50/p90/p99 and kv-hit% before we push.

kai: On it. Kicking off canary now. :eyes:

[kai later]
kai: Canary numbers (revert applied): p99 22.6ms (baseline 22.3), p50 3.1ms, kv_hit 86.1% — looks good, throughput back to baseline.

rob: Great. I'll open the cherry-pick/backport PR to the release branch and request a patch verify + QA smoke.

anya: Also let's add a perf-unit test for KV hit-rate under varied batching. Filed: #4205

maria: After PR merges we'll run a small canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%, rollback policy in place.

rob: Thanks team. I'll post a brief note in #incidents and ping customer success about possible impact window. :shipit:
